historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is unusable: FY2022 'equity' is Danaher's net parent investment ($3,240M), cut to $1,389M at FY2023 by the ~$2.6B spin distribution, then rebuilt to $3,106M by FY2025 -- a 2yr equity CAGR of ~50% that measures the spin, not compounding. Revenue CAGR selected instead.
historical_growth.notes: Only FY2021-FY2025 annuals exist (FY2021-23 carve-out/combined), so 5yr CAGRs are null and 4yr (FY21-25) is shown. Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC - equity-award withholding taxes (withholding pre-FY2023 undisclosed, taken as 0). Owner-FCF CAGR (5.3% 3yr) trails reported (6.6%) only modestly: SBC rose from $41M to $74M (0.8% -> 1.3% of revenue) post-spin. Carve-out FY2021-23 FCF and EPS bore no standalone interest cost (~$137M/yr cash interest since the 2023 notes) or full standalone corporate cost, so the post-spin series understates the underlying trend; EPS FY2024 dip is that effect.

scenario_narratives.base: Guidance year delivered: FY2026 core growth 3-4.5% with H2 acceleration to 5-6%, reported ~+7% including In-Situ and GlobalVision, adjusted operating margin +25-50bp. Thereafter Water Quality grows mid-single-digit on data-centre cooling/industrial water and regulation-driven testing while China municipal stays soft; PQI tracks packaging volumes at ~3% helped by Esko/GlobalVision software. VES productivity lifts pre-SBC EBITDA margin ~30bp/yr from 26.2% to a 28% plateau. Growth fades to 3% by year 10; terminal 2.5% at 8.5%, capped at 18x.
scenario_narratives.bull: Data-centre and industrial water-scarcity demand turn Water Quality into a 6-7% organic grower, PQI digital workflow (Esko, AI-augmented GlobalVision) lifts recurring mix above 62%, and ChemTreat raw-material pressure eases so pricing sticks. Margin expands ~50bp/yr toward 29.5% (Danaher-style VES compounding). Growth fades from 6.5% to 3.5%; terminal 3% with a 20x cap.
scenario_narratives.bear: FY2026 is largely booked (H1 +7.1%), but from 2027 China/high-growth municipal water funding stays broken, an industrial/consumer slowdown hits PQI coding and marking volumes, and Xylem/Ecolab/Pentair competition plus ChemTreat input-cost volatility and tariffs cap pricing. Organic growth 2-3%, margin slips to 25.5% and never recovers, cash tax drifts to 21.5%. Terminal 2% with a 15x cap. Not a solvency case: leverage is ~1x EBITDA.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A Danaher-lineage compounder of recurring consumables, chemistry and software revenue: the value is in steady mid-single-digit organic growth and VES-driven margin creep, not in M&A. The model therefore projects organic growth only and treats bolt-ons as NPV-neutral, so any value they create is upside to these numbers.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal value is ~60-70% of EV; a 1pp WACC move swings value ~15-20%.
China/high-growth municipal water funding and PQI industrial volumes drive the gap between base and bear.
Bolt-on M&A (Cleanwater1 $465M pending) is excluded; overpaying would destroy value the model does not see, and accretive deals add value it does not count.
ChemTreat raw-material volatility and tariffs (with uncertain refund timing) can absorb a year of VES margin expansion.

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow add-back $74M (XBRL ShareBasedCompensation) + $13M taxes withheld on net-share settlement (XBRL AdjustmentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation); Veralto publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed.

inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Cost of equity 9.0% = 4.2% 10y UST + beta ~0.95 x 5.0% ERP (defensive water/consumables mix, ~62% recurring revenue). After-tax cost of debt ~3.9% (5.0% pre-tax on IG notes x (1-21%)). Debt ~13% of EV at market (3.4B vs ~23.2B mkt cap). WACC ~8.3%, rounded to 8.5%. Same WACC in every scenario: risk is charged in the scenario paths and weights, not twice.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842: operating lease cost ($210M liability) already sits inside operating profit/EBITDA, so leases are in the flows; lease liabilities NOT added to net debt (single treatment).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing row 'Operating company'); Veralto is a US analytics/instrument + consumables + water-treatment chemistry business with no bank, REIT, holdco or insurance features. No prior DCF or memory entry -- fresh build. Ten-year horizon because margins still expand ~25-50bp/yr under VES. BASE REVENUE is FY2025 ($5,503M); the FY2026 growth step (+7%) includes In-Situ (Q1-26) and GlobalVision (Apr-26, $195M), whose $620M cash cost has ALREADY left the balance sheet (H1-26 cash flow), so their revenue is consistent with the net-debt anchor. From FY2027 growth is ORGANIC only: bolt-on M&A revenue is not projected because its acquisition capital is not deducted. PENDING Cleanwater1 (~$465M, ~$135M LTM sales, expected Q4-26 close) is excluded on both sides (assumed bought at fair value, NPV-neutral). EBITDA margin is pre-SBC (FY25: op profit 1,277 + D&A 78 + SBC 74 = 1,429 / 5,503 = 26.0%; H1-26 25.8% after ~30bp transaction costs). D&A includes acquired-intangible amortisation (FY25 1.4%, H1-26 1.8% after the acquisitions). Cash tax on unlevered EBIT ~20.5% (FY25 cash taxes paid $235M; GAAP ETR 19.9%; H1-26 18.9%). Working capital capture is NEGATIVE: receivables + inventory exceed payables + deferred revenue, so growth consumes cash. Interest income not stripped: Veralto is net-debt ($1.26B) and reports interest net. base.narrative: FY26 lands at guidance (core +3-4.5%, ~+7% reported with In-Situ/GlobalVision, margin +25-50bp); organic growth then runs ~4.5% fading to 3% -- in line with the 4.2% FY22-25 revenue CAGR -- and VES adds ~30bp/yr of margin to a 28% pre-SBC EBITDA plateau.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): China municipal water weakness and PQI volume cyclicality are live today, and core growth has run only 3-4.5% for two years. Base 55%: guidance was raised twice in 2026, ~62% recurring revenue and ~1x leverage make the central path the most evidenced. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): it needs both a sustained Water Quality acceleration and ~50bp/yr margin expansion with benign raw materials -- several independent things going right.
